bull.b: Minimal leverage and a substantially expanded capital base provide financial flexibility for clinical development. This reduces near-term balance-sheet risk and gives Oruka more capacity to fund programs or pursue partnerships.

Hiring a dermatology and immunology commercialization veteran strengthens preparation for potential product launches. It may improve future market-access, launch-planning and partnering capabilities as clinical assets advance.

A broader licensed field increases the potential applications and strategic flexibility of the IL-23 platform, including ORKA-001. This could support development optionality and future partnering across multiple indications.

bear.b: Oruka has no recurring product revenue because its therapies remain in clinical development. Until commercialization or partnering inflows emerge, the company lacks an operating revenue base to offset research, development and corporate costs.

Expanding losses indicate that development spending is increasing ahead of any commercial return. Continued deterioration in profitability can pressure capital efficiency and raise the funding required before clinical assets generate meaningful economic value.

The worsening cash outflow increases dependence on future financing, equity issuance or partnering proceeds. Even with low debt, sustained clinical spending could reduce financial flexibility if programs take longer to advance or monetization is delayed.
